statement: The project is an unbranded OCD-style overdrive clone (v0.1), not branded as Fulltone/OCD.
Target supply is 5–18V DC center-negative and true bypass is required.
OCD-style reference topology uses TL082 dual op-amp gain stages with MOSFET+Ge asymmetric clipping referenced to a floating Vref (~Vcc/2) in common v1.4+ implementations.
conditions: v1.4-style reference; exact component values revision-dependent

statement: OCD soft-slope clipping character should be attributed primarily to topology (series resistor + floating Vref network), not to an intrinsically softer 2N7000 body diode.
For complex musical signals, asymmetric clipping explanations must not reduce to a simple even-harmonics-equals-warm rule; IMD and waveform/envelope behavior matter.
Increasing single-supply voltage (e.g., 9V to 18V) increases available op-amp swing/headroom around Vref, all else equal.
conditions: single-supply Vref-biased op-amp stages; device limits apply
locator: general op-amp headroom; verify per TL082 datasheet limits

statement: Vref divider example (ideal) 100k/100k at 9V yields 4.5V with Thevenin resistance ~50k.

Genuine 1N34A germanium diodes are variable and often hard to source reliably; Schottky diodes (e.g., BAT41/BAT46) are common substitutes in some designs but have different Vf/leakage and may alter clipping character.
2N7000 and TL082 are generally readily available through major distributors in common packages; availability still depends on chosen package/vendor and should be checked at BOM time.

TI TL082 product parametric summary (S007, opened 2026-11-09) indicates total supply min 7V, input common-mode headroom to negative supply typ 3V, output swing headroom typ 1.5V per rail; exact conditions must be verified in SLOS081O.

statement: C4/C8 feedback fix (D_FB_FIX): C4 moved in series with R5 (X1_FB->X1_RG->VREF) and C8 in series with R11 (X3_FB->X3_RG->VREF). Prior parallel placement gave zero DC feedback and saturated both op-amps (old X1_OUT=X3_OUT=1.523V at 9V). Series placement gives unity DC gain + AC bass limit; verified OP at 8/9/18V: VREF 3.588/4.039/7.947V, X1_OUT 2.441/2.747/5.406V, X3_OUT 2.538/2.857/5.905V (without LED load).

AC excitation split: V_IN (SIN transient) + V_AC (1V AC) in series because the spec generator drops AC magnitude when a waveform is present. Verified AC results at 9V: OUT 37.23dB pre-fix baseline invalid (zero AC); post-fix gain measurable.

Added reverse-polarity protection D_PWR (1N5819 series Schottky, APPROX model), status LED D_LED + R_LED 4.7k from VCC_F to GND (always-on in sim, physically switched by 3PDT), 9V battery via switching DC jack + input-jack battery disconnect, and explicit HP/LP SW1. 8V protection margin ~0.7V above TL082 7V min is a bench gate (P-FET fallback if it fails).

Tone-stack corrected per S002 text/image: X4=10k tone pot wired as rheostat in series with C11 to ground (treble-to-ground shunt from TONE_TOP); R14=22k/R15=33k from TONE_TOP to volume path; HP=closed (R15 parallel R14, brighter per S003), LP=open (R14 only, darker). Reverses provisional D_TONE label.

statement: v0.4 merged spec verifies clean: verify.py 13 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed; required design/limits/measurements/simulate PASS. 9V nominal (Drive/Tone/Volume 50%, LP, 100k load): gain 44.57dB @1kHz, passband width 1369Hz, THD 66.3%, output noise 141µV, output 0.690Vrms. All metrics exploratory (no verified reference targets); not a verified OCD clone claim.

Supply-corner matrix (nominal pots, 50mVpk 1kHz): VREF tracks ~VCC_F/2 at 8/9/18V (3.427/3.867/7.723V vs VCC_F/2 3.461/3.906/7.917V), no op-amp saturation (X1_OUT=X1_P, X3_OUT=X3_P at each corner). HP vs LP midband gain essentially identical at 1kHz (tone control affects HF, not midband); THD lower at 18V (35-37%) vs 8/9V (62-66%). 18V midband gain drop (22.2dB vs 44.6dB) is a clip-bias/threshold sensitivity, not an op-amp artifact (see C042); bench-verify.

Two circuit-design-skill fixes applied: (1) ngspice_raw.find_plot('tran') word-boundary match (was matching 'DC transfer characteristic', breaking output_vrms); (2) verify.py re-runs ngspice without -r when '.fourier line ignored since rawfile was produced', restoring THD measurement.

Prior saturated-bias results (X1_OUT/X3_OUT=1.523V at 9V, from C4/C8 in parallel with R5/R11) and zero-AC results (V_IN with SIN waveform and no AC magnitude) are superseded; do not cite as evidence. Corrected by C034/C035.

statement: 18V AC-gain collapse (44.57 dB at 8/9V vs 22.24 dB at 18V) is caused by the clip network, not the op-amps: M1 is diode-connected from VREF to CLIP_A, so Vgs=VREF-CLIP_A is ratiometric (~0.3*VREF) and crosses the APPROX_2N7000 VTO=2.1V at 18V, shunting CLIP_A (CLIP_A/X1_OUT 0.820 -> 0.059). VTO sensitivity at 18V: 1.5->17.6dB, 2.1->22.2dB, >=2.5->44.6dB; at 9V all VTO give 44.6dB. Real behavior depends on 2N7000 Vgs(th) (0.8-3.0V, S008) and the exact bias; bench-verify (K2). Refines C039's 'model artifact' label.

2N7000 in TO-92 (onsemi CASE 135AN) has pin 1 = Source, pin 2 = Gate, pin 3 = Drain, and Vgs(th) min/typ/max = 0.8/2.1/3.0 V. This fixes the TO-92 footprint pad map as d=3, g=2, s=1, bulk tied to source (pad 1).
conditions: onsemi NDS7002A datasheet, TO-92 package drawing

statement: KiCad Device:D and Device:LED number pin 1 = K (cathode) and pin 2 = A (anode), while SPICE diode nodes are ordered (anode, cathode). The correct implicit PCB default is therefore [2,1], not [1,2]; D_PWR, D1 and D_LED resolve as anode->pad 2, cathode->pad 1.
conditions: KiCad official footprint library, master branch

statement: CUI/Same Sky PJ-102AH: pad 1 = center pin, pad 2 = sleeve, pad 3 = switch. The switch is normally closed between pads 2 and 3 with no plug and opens when a plug is inserted, so wiring pad 2 = VCC_JACK, pad 3 = BAT_POS, pad 1 = GND gives center-negative DC input and disconnects the battery when a DC plug is present.
conditions: PJ-102AH datasheet schematic plus distributor switch description

statement: Taiwan Alpha RD901F-40-00D mono potentiometer uses pin 1 and pin 3 as the fixed element ends and pin 2 as the wiper. statement: The stereo input jack Neutrik NMJ6HFD2 exposes pads R,S,T,RN,SN,TN and the mono output jack NMJ4HFD2 exposes S,T,SN,TN. Using T = signal tip, S = ground and R = battery negative lets a mono TS plug short the ring to the sleeve, connecting the battery only while a plug is inserted.
